subtopic: Expected Value and Variance of a Random Variable
stem: Find the mean and variance of the number randomly selected from 1 to 15.
solution:
The sample space of the experiment is \(S = \{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 15\}\).

Let \(X\) denote the number selected.

Then \(X\) is a random variable which can take values 1, 2, 3, \(\ldots\), 15. Each number selected is equiprobable therefore

\(P(1) = P(2) = P(3) = \ldots = P(15) = \dfrac{1}{15}\)

\(\mu = E(X) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i p_i = 1 \times \dfrac{1}{15} + 2 \times \dfrac{1}{15} + 3 \times \dfrac{1}{15} + \ldots + 15 \times \dfrac{1}{15}\)

\(= (1 + 2 + 3 + \ldots + 15) \times \dfrac{1}{15} = \left(\dfrac{15 \times 16}{2}\right) \times \dfrac{1}{15} = 8\)

\(Var(X) = \left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i^2 p_i\right) - \left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i p_i\right)^2 = 1^2 \times \dfrac{1}{15} + 2^2 \times \dfrac{1}{15} + 3^2 \times \dfrac{1}{15} + \ldots + 15^2 \times \dfrac{1}{15} - (8)^2\)

\(= (1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 + \ldots + 15^2) \times \dfrac{1}{15} - (8)^2\)

\(= \left(\dfrac{15 \times 16 \times 31}{6}\right) \times \dfrac{1}{15} - (8)^2\)

\(= 82.67 - 64 = 18.67\)

subtopic: Expected Value and Variance of a Random Variable
stem: Two cards are drawn simultaneously (or successively without replacement) from a well shuffled pack of 52 cards. Find the mean, variance and standard deviation of the number of kings drawn.
solution:
Let \(X\) denote the number of kings in a draw of two cards. \(X\) is a random variable which can assume the values 0, 1 or 2.

Then \(P(X = 0) = P(\text{no card is king}) = \dfrac{{}^{48}C_2}{{}^{52}C_2} = \dfrac{48 \times 47}{52 \times 51} = \dfrac{188}{221}\)

Then \(P(X = 1) = P(\text{exactly one card is king}) = \dfrac{{}^{4}C_1 \times {}^{48}C_1}{{}^{52}C_2} = \dfrac{4 \times 48 \times 27}{52 \times 51} = \dfrac{32}{221}\)

Then \(P(X = 2) = P(\text{both cards are king}) = \dfrac{{}^{4}C_2}{{}^{52}C_2} = \dfrac{4 \times 3}{52 \times 51} = \dfrac{1}{221}\)

\(\mu = E(X) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i p_i = 0 \times \dfrac{188}{221} + 1 \times \dfrac{32}{221} + 2 \times \dfrac{1}{221} = \dfrac{34}{221}\)

\(Var(X) = \left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i^2 p_i\right) - \left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i p_i\right)^2 = \left(0^2 \times \dfrac{188}{221} + 1^2 \times \dfrac{32}{221} + 2^2 \times \dfrac{1}{221}\right) - \left(\dfrac{34}{221}\right)^2\)

\(= \dfrac{36}{221} - \dfrac{1156}{48841} = \dfrac{6800}{48841} = 0.1392\)

\(\sigma = \sqrt{Var(X)} = \sqrt{0.1392}\)
